clue.text: Study-group for factory dance

parts.note: a works is a factory or industrial plant
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A request for a group to study a factory dance, as if workers had a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar where a group meets to discuss and practise a subject is called by this name.

clue.text: In this address one gets nothing on dole

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: nothing is the round letter O, like zero
a dole is a portion handed out, a ration

explanation.surface: Claimants told that this address is where you get nothing on the dole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is a speech, not a home; 'on' in a down clue puts O above RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public speech.

clue.text: Child named as likely to win a book

parts.note: a kid is a child
a tipster's nap is the day's best bet, so a horse napped is named as the likely winner

explanation.surface: A child is tipped to win a book prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidnapped is Robert Louis Stevenson's novel; 'nap' is British racing slang for a tipster's most confident pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A Robert Louis Stevenson adventure novel of 1886.

clue.text: Starving country has no short answer

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe
A is short for answer

explanation.surface: A starving nation finds itself with no quick reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Very much in need of food.

clue.text: It may be used to buy oneself out of trouble

definitions.text: It may be used to buy oneself out of trouble

parts.words: It may be used to buy oneself out of trouble
parts.note: reads like a bribe or bail, but means payment extorted by gangsters who threaten harm unless paid

explanation.walkthrough: The trouble is the one the gangsters will cause themselves if not paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash extorted by racketeers in return for not harming a business.

clue.text: Entrance visa produced in the right hand

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the abbreviation for right hand
produced suggests the letters of visa are worked into something new

explanation.surface: An entry visa is pulled out and held in the right hand at a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like the noun for a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to enchant or carry away with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to enrapture or delight them, the old literary sense of the verb.

clue.text: Beads, mostly, on chap who shows his bloomers?

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the first piece above the second
mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rosary is a string of prayer beads
Ian is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man in prayer beads who displays his baggy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like old knickers; they are flowers. 'mostly' cuts ROSARY to ROSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A grower of roses who exhibits them at flower shows.

clue.text: Disinclination to move train that is shunted?

indicators.note: shunted suggests rolling stock pushed into a new arrangement

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A train that is moved onto a siding seems reluctant to go anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendency of a body to stay at rest; sluggishness.

clue.text: Am at home suffering with a hard swelling

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are distressed into another shape

explanation.surface: Someone stays home in pain from a hard lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges AMATHOME into HAEMATOM, and the clue's 'a' ends it; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid mass of clotted blood under the skin, a bruise-like swelling.

clue.text: Our England is a — that is full of stately views" (Kipling)

definitions.text: Our England is a — that is full of stately views" (Kipling)

parts.words: Our England is a — that is full of stately views" (Kipling)
parts.note: the opening line of a Kipling poem, with its key noun left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the poem is Kipling's 'The Glory of the Garden', whose first line the clue quotes with the missing word blanked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem compares England to a cultivated plot of flower beds and lawns, so the missing noun is that plot.

clue.text: Old hat of Leo's to be restored

indicators.note: restored hints that these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: the name Leo with its possessive s, all used as letters

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned belonging to Leo is going to be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges LEOSTOBE; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of date, no longer in use or fashion.

clue.text: Run counter to girl's consent

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, and the possessive adds S
to agree is to consent

explanation.surface: A girl's agreement is somehow at odds with something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To differ or conflict with something is to run counter to it.

clue.text: Platforms for some of Cairo's trains

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Railway platforms for some of the trains in Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised stands for public speakers are called by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Bird to shoot from cover

explanation.surface: A hunter takes aim at a bird from a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird with a long bill; also a verb for firing at someone from a hidden position, as a sniper does.

clue.text: Producer of -Psycho" required worker to be a yes-man

indicators.note: something that produces the word Psycho can be read as rearranging it

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: Hitchcock, who produced Psycho, needed a staff member who would agree with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The producer is not Hitchcock: 'Producer of' rearranges PSYCHO into SYCOPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning flatterer who agrees with a superior to win favour.

clue.text: In which the subject of torture is dropped

definitions.text: In which the subject of torture is dropped

parts.words: In which the subject of torture is dropped
parts.note: reads like a story where a topic of conversation is abandoned, but describes a punishment in which the victim is hauled up and let fall

explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks like a topic of talk; it is the person suffering, who is hoisted by the wrists on a rope and dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical punishment of hoisting a victim by a rope and letting them fall partway, jerking the arms.

clue.text: Abnormal fluttering, but it does not appear in medical examination

indicators.note: does not appear says the word it is removed

parts.note: palpitation is irregular fluttering of the heart
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's check-up in which irregular heartbeats fail to show.
explanation.definitionFit: Examination by touch, the doctor feeling the body with the hands.

clue.text: Arab, male, perhaps, high in Israel

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: Sion is a variant of Zion, a name for Israel
tall means high

explanation.surface: An Arab man, perhaps, stands tall in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is the horse breed, not a person: an Arab male horse may be a stallion.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, and an Arab is a breed of horse.

clue.text: State rider?

explanation.surface: A question about someone riding a horse on behalf of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: One's state of health or repair, and a proviso added to an agreement, as a rider is a clause tacked on.

clue.text: Breathing-space below the bridge

parts.note: reads like a gap under a river crossing, but the bridge is the bony ridge of the nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' is the bridge of the nose; 'breathing-space' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two openings in the nose through which air passes.

clue.text: Hail-and-farewell originally given to cook, we hear

definitions.text: Hail-and-farewell originally given to cook, we hear

parts.words: Hail-and-farewell originally given to cook, we hear
parts.note: a greeting that also means goodbye, said to have first greeted Captain Cook when he reached Hawaii

explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is Captain James Cook, the explorer who landed in Hawaii, not a kitchen worker; 'we hear' means 'reportedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word used both for welcoming and for parting.

clue.text: Bent wire useful in locks?

parts.note: suggests a burglar's tool for picking door locks, but the locks are locks of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' tempts toward lock-picking; the wire holds hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped clip that holds a hairstyle in place.

clue.text: Mystery of Churchill's red outer wrapping

definitions.text: Mystery of Churchill's red outer wrapping

parts.words: Mystery of Churchill's red outer wrapping
parts.note: recalls Churchill calling Russia a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside a further puzzle, the outermost layer

explanation.walkthrough: Churchill in 1939 called Russia a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside a final, outermost puzzle; 'red' is Soviet Russia, and that outer wrapping is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something puzzling and inexplicable, a mystery.

clue.text: Falstaff's follower expected to go off?

explanation.surface: Falstaff's sidekick is expected to leave at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare's Henry IV and Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering companion of Falstaff in Shakespeare, and a handgun, which is meant to fire.

clue.text: Chinese official in a loose jacket

explanation.surface: A Chinese bureaucrat dressed in a baggy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bureaucrat of imperial China, and a loose high-collared garment named after such officials.

clue.text: An undergarment is back to front and worn, causing a scraped area

parts.note: the article gives one letter
a bra is a woman's undergarment

indicators.note: back to front says the word is is turned round

parts.note: clothes worn are on

explanation.surface: Someone wears a piece of underwear the wrong way round and it chafes the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A graze is skin scraped away by rubbing.

clue.text: Influenza case to take physical exercise, initially

parts.note: a grip is a travelling bag or holdall

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Advice that a flu sufferer should pack a bag and go and work out.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word, from French, for flu.

clue.text: Last we see of a crab in Solent, it turns out

definitions.text: Last we see of a crab

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters of Solent come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A crab's final glimpse in the waters off southern England, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England. 'it turns out' rearranges SOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail fan or last segment of a crustacean's body is its rear end, the final part seen as it goes.

clue.text: Longing to become youth leader with a salary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a salary is what one is earning

explanation.surface: A young person yearns to become a leader with a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep desire or pining for something.
